title: Absent overdue-since date yields delinquent day-count zero, not an error or epoch value (loan 3)
_note: Parity vector transcribing the ABSENT-date row of the delinquency block read back for SEED-L03 at business date 2026-09-01 under tenant gerege. The read-back carries no summary.overdueSinceDate and no delinquent.pastDueDate / delinquent.delinquentDate, and the delinquent block reads pastDueDays 0 and delinquentDays 0. request.delinquency therefore OMITS overdue_since_date (omitempty) and carries only the business date; expect.overdue_days and expect.delinquent_days are "0". This vector exists to discriminate a port that treats a missing overdue-since date as fatal, or as the zero time (1970-01-01) and so reports a days-since-epoch value, instead of returning zero [delinquency.go:96,101-103]. It is kept in preference to the OTHER absent row (SEED-L06, same absent date and same zero counts) because the two carry one fact: loan L06 is NOT cloned here. WHAT THIS ROW DOES NOT GRADE: the paused/grace subtraction and the negative clamp, for the same reasons as the non-zero rows. TIME ZONE: the absent row takes no date at all, so it cannot exercise the zone resolution; the non-zero rows use bare midnight-aligned civil dates, so none of the committed rows discriminates a UTC-vs-Asia/Ulaanbaatar parse defect. Say that rather than claim the zone is covered.

provenance.note: Both expected cells are transcribed from the committed SEED-L03 loan detail read-back loan-3-detail-raw.json, whose delinquent.pastDueDays and delinquent.delinquentDays are both 0. The same file has NO summary.overdueSinceDate key and no delinquent.pastDueDate / delinquent.delinquentDate key, which is why request.delinquency omits overdue_since_date; the absence is the observed fact, not a synthesised one. The business date 2026-09-01 is the corpus BUSINESS_DATE pinned separately in the seed businessdate capture, cited below. The capture is a single-line JSON document (wc -l = 0), so every observation is at line 1.
provenance.citation: loan-3-detail-raw.json:1 (single-line committed read-back, tenant gerege): summary has NO overdueSinceDate key, and delinquent {"pastDueDays":0,"nextPaymentDueDate":[2026,7,1],...,"delinquentDays":0,"delinquentAmount":0,...,"delinquencyPausePeriods":[]} has NO pastDueDate and NO delinquentDate. Business date 2026-09-01: .softhouse/capture/seed/out/businessdate-get-raw.json:1 "type":"BUSINESS_DATE","date":[2026,9,1]. With no overdue-since date there are 0 overdue days, hence 0 delinquent days, and the oracle reports zero rather than refusing or returning a days-since-epoch value.
